hook_text: On 1 December 1834, slavery ended at the Cape. Or did it?
clip_script: Thirty-nine thousand people at the Cape woke up on 1 December 1834 legally free. But there was a catch: they had to keep working for their former owners, unpaid, as apprentices for four more years. And the British government paid compensation, to the owners. The enslaved got nothing. On 1 December 1838, apprenticeship finally ended. Freed people celebrated in Cape Town and on mission stations. Many walked off the farms for good, to towns and to places like Genadendal. Freedom had come, but without land, money or fair wages, the struggle wasn't over.
visual_style: A calendar flips to 1 December 1834, then to 1 December 1838; a crowd gathers outside a mission church; a family walks along a road away from a farm.
pacing: A hook, a twist, a celebration, a sober close.
